paper.title_en: A note on Positivity and Rigidity for an Expanding Quasi-Local Energy
paper.abstract_en: We study positivity and rigidity for an expanding quasi-local energy $E_λ$ associated with constantly umbilic initial data $(Ω,g,k=λg)$, introduced in earlier work [ALP26] as an analogue of the Brown-York energy adapted to an expanding flat de Sitter background. Under nonnegative scalar curvature and suitable boundary assumptions, our previous results established positivity for $λ$ below a geometrically determined threshold $α$, while vanishing $E_λ$ at $λ=α$ forced the boundary to be round. In this paper, we strengthen this endpoint rigidity statement by showing that, if $E_λ=0$ when $λ=α$, then $(Ω,g)$ is isometric to a closed Euclidean 3-ball of radius at most $1/λ$. The proof combines the rigidity theorem of Shi-Tam for the Brown-York energy with a strict concavity argument. We also construct an explicit counterexample to the positivity and rigidity conjecture formulated in [ALP26], showing that the energy can become negative beyond this threshold and that vanishing energy need not imply rigidity.
